subject: Ephemeral keystore handshake and review plan

From: Emily Park <emily.park@cygnus-audit.com>

Cc: FinCo DevOps <devops@finco.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Apr 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: SDLC evidence ask — ephemeral keystore handoff narrative

Hi Marcus,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of FinCo's SIG intake we're creating a short narrative that explains Redwood's ephemeral keystore/handshake flow for rotating customer-facing HSM/KMS keys during canary rollouts. The assessor team has asked for:

- A concise written narrative describing the handoff between CI, deploy orchestration, and the keystore rotation process (who signs what, RBAC checks).
- A sample rotation log showing one rotation event (timestamps, operator id, runbook link).
- Proof that canary rollouts are gated (CI job IDs, policy name, and failure rollback behavior).

Can you share the narrative and any artifacts by EOD Tuesday (2028-04-11)? If there are any PII or sensitive fields we should expect to redact, please call those out.

Emily Park
Senior Assessor, Cygnus Audit
emily.park@cygnus-audit.com

On behalf of FinCo Security Team

Emily —

Acknowledged. Looping in Irene (platform security) and Kimberly (release engineering) to assemble the narrative and artifacts. A couple quick clarifying questions so we deliver precisely what you need:

1) For the "handshake" narrative, do you want an operator-level sequence (console/API calls + service principals + audit events) or an abstracted diagram-level narrative?
2) Is the sample rotation log required to be unredacted (we will remove token values and customer IDs), or is a redacted event acceptable for the SIG pack?

We will prepare: a 1-page narrative, a redacted rotation log, and the canary gating playbook excerpt. If you need CI job IDs from FinCo's side (for cross-reference), tagging FinCo DevOps in case they want to help with correlation logs.

—Marcus

Emily — quick update and proposed delivery:

What we'll deliver (target: 2028-04-11 EOD):
- 1-page operator-level narrative describing the keystore handshake and RBAC checks (who calls the deploy API, how the orchestrator requests fresh ephemeral keys, where HSM/KMS custody transfers occur).
- Redacted rotation log CSV (timestamps, operator_id, job_id, outcome).
- Canary gating excerpt (policy name: deploy.canary_gate_v2, CI job: build-and-deploy/canary), plus the canary rollback summary.
- Links to internal runbook and an index spreadsheet with artifact locations.

Attachments in this thread will include the redacted rotation log and the canary playbook excerpt for context — they are samples only. We will not include raw key material. If Cygnus needs a full unredacted audit for an in-person review, we can arrange a secured session with the security team and evidence redaction controls.

Irene, Kimberly: please see the action items below.

Marcus

Subject: Re: SDLC evidence ask — ephemeral keystore handoff narrative

Hi all — attaching the sample artifacts referenced (keystore_rotation_log_20280408.csv and canary_rollout_playbook_v3.pdf). Notes:

- Narrative summary (operator-level):
  * Trigger: CI finishes preflight tests and posts an approved artifact to the deploy queue (CI job id included in log).
  * Orchestrator (orchd) requests ephemeral key material from the internal KMS agent via a signed service principal call (service account: infra/orchd@redwood).
  * KMS responds with ephemeral credentials; the orchestrator writes the minimal keystore entry and performs a signed rotation action recorded in audit.log (audit event id included).
  * RBAC: rotation actions must be authorized by role: deploy_operator and keystore_admin. Approvals are enforced at the orchestration layer; manual approvals are recorded in the runbook checklist.

- Where artifacts live:
  * Rotation logs: secure S3 bucket (s3://redwood-evidence/rotation-logs/) — indexes are in the attached spreadsheet (sdlc_evidence_index_2028-04-09.xlsx).
  * Playbooks: internal Drive -> /secure-sdlc/canary/ (link provided).
  * CI job traces: link to the job id in Cloud CI; job ids are redacted in this sample but available under NDA.

- Canary failure behavior: if canary health probes fail >3 consecutive checks within a 10-minute window, the rollout is automatically rolled back and an incident is opened. The canary gating policy id is deploy.canary_gate_v2 (referenced in policy store).

Redaction note: the attached CSV has token values replaced with <REDACTED>, operator IDs are internal UUIDs (kept), and customer identifiers are masked. If the assessor requires unredacted logs we can provide a time-limited access session under a controlled viewing policy.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Principal Platform Security Engineer
Redwood Inference
